decisions.executionNote: Raise and pitch right gripper toward the red mouse, using small continuous elbow-up approach increments; mouse depth remains approximate.

Replan from executed prefix with smaller translation increments, descending while approaching pad to maintain joint continuity and extension margin.
Avoid further reach extension: retract wrist slightly and tip held mouse forward over the pad, then release; mouse has rotated in the jaws.

Continue sliding the keyboard toward its outline, advancing the right corner slightly more to remove the visible yaw.

Release the centered keyboard and lift clear. Move left toward the cactus figurine while retracting the right arm on its own side.
Align the left open jaws toward the cactus stem with clearance; finish withdrawing the right arm. The clock was displaced and will be relocalized later.

Make a small leftward placement correction, release the cactus onto the stand, and withdraw gently to inspect stability.

Align the left gripper vertically and descend over the clock face, using the wrist view to keep the clock between the open jaws.

Lift the clock clear and translate left toward the drawer, with slight retraction to preserve reach margin; confirm the clock follows the jaws.

Descend more deeply with open jaws around the clock body, correcting slightly right; inspect before closing to avoid another shallow grasp.
Descent met contact, so stop lowering. Close around the clock at the observed pose and test retention with a slow vertical lift.
Clock slipped right rather than being retained. Reopen, recenter the jaws over its displaced body, and approach again without closing prematurely.
Use the wrist image to center the clock farther between the jaws, correcting the tool-to-EE offset before another grasp.
Clock is now centered between the jaws. Close fully at the observed contact height and lift a few centimeters to verify retention visually.
Clock remains on the table after the test. Reopen and descend farther around its sides in small increments rather than repeating the shallow closure.
Unload the contact and change grasp yaw to match the clock's diagonal sides; retract slightly away from the cactus before reapproaching.
Adjust yaw in the opposite direction to reduce corner interference and lower the open jaws around the clock body.
Square the jaws with the clock's lower edge and descend carefully for a deeper side grasp, avoiding its diagonal corners.
Relieve the left jaw's corner interference with a small lateral correction, close on the squared clock body, and test with a short lift.

Replan below the reach limit: lower with a slight retraction and straighten the approach axis, keeping the clock centered inside the open jaws.

Approach the clock at an intermediate fore-aft alignment, lower slightly below its upper edges, and close without immediately translating.

Raise the retained clock above the drawer rim and shift left over its top. Maintain a slightly forward-pitched grasp to keep the wrist within reach.

Refine handle height from the wrist view and advance slowly before closing at the deeper engagement point.
